title: add NVTX ranges, counters, and microbench harness for runtime profiling (batching/KV cache/kernels)
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: We need higher-fidelity visibility into runtime hotspots affecting continuous batching, KV cache behavior, and kernel scheduling. Existing telemetry (trace spans and basic metrics) was insufficient to correlate GPU kernels, batching decisions, and KV cache hits/misses at the per-request level. This PR adds lightweight NVTX ranges around key runtime phases, exposes aggregated counters for microbench harnesses, and ships a microbench target to exercise batching and KV cache patterns so we can reproduce and quantify regressions and optimizations.

Changes (high level):
- Add nvtx wrapper utilities and scoped NVTX ranges to runtime hot paths (request scheduling, batch formation, dispatch to execution, post-dispatch aggregation).
- Instrument KV cache with miss/hit counters and timing ranges (cache lookup, cache insert).
- Emit batching metrics: observed batch_size distribution, wait_time_for_batch, and per-batch token counts.
- Add a small microbenchmark harness under tools/microbench that can replay synthetic request arrival patterns (poisson, bursty, steady) and measure NVTX annotations + aggregated counters.
- Add a perf dashboard JSON (dashboards/perf/nvtx-batching.json) to visualize NVTX ranges exported via our perf exporter and to correlate with existing latency/cost charts.
- Unit tests for nvtx utils and a CI job that runs the microbench in a lightweight mode (CPU-only emulation) to prevent flakiness on PRs.

Why NVTX: NVTX ranges let us connect CPU-side scheduling decisions with GPU kernel execution windows and easily annotate traces captured by perf tools (nsight, cupy/profiler, or perf exporter). The scoped ranges are cheap when NVTX is disabled at runtime.

Checklist: 
- [x] NVTX utility and scoped annotations added
- [x] KV cache counters and timing ranges added
- [x] Microbench harness implemented with configurable arrival distributions and workloads
- [x] Perf dashboard included and documented
- [x] Tests for utility functions and CI microbench smoke job
- [x] Documentation in docs/perf/instrumentation.md

Testing and results: 
- Local microbench (RTX A5000, 16GB) with synthetic steady traffic (QPS=200, tokens/request=64) showed:
  - 8-12% reduction in tail debug noise after applying more aggressive kernel selection (measured with NVTX ranges to exclude scheduling jitter)
  - Batch size distribution captured as expected; uncovered a corner-case where single-request batches were created at 1.9ms wait threshold instead of 2.5ms (root cause in scheduler heuristic, follow-up PR planned).
- CI: new microbench smoke job runs in CPU-emulation mode and passes on linux-x86.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- The dashboard (dashboards/perf/nvtx-batching.json) consumes exported NVTX range durations and the new batching/KV cache counters. It provides per-model filters and a grouped view for batch formation latency vs. kernel execution latency.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag REDWOOD_PROFILING_NVTX (disabled by default).
- Enable on perf-canary and benchmark-lab for 48 hours and collect traces.
- If dashboards show stable results, enable default opt-in for engineering org.

Related: ENG-4123 for investigation, PERF-231 for dashboard design.

Notes: The NVTX annotations are guarded by runtime config and are no-op when NVTX is not available. This PR does not change any public API, and the feature is controlled by flags and env vars in deployments.

Add dashboard json and docs (dashboards/perf/nvtx-batching.json, docs/perf/instrumentation.md)

release_notes: Adds optional NVTX profiling ranges and a microbenchmark harness to better diagnose runtime batching, KV cache, and kernel scheduling performance. Feature is behind REDWOOD_PROFILING_NVTX and disabled by default.
notes: Follow-up PRs planned: scheduler heuristic fix (small change to wait threshold), benchmark-lab wiring for automated trace uploads, and a performance regression test using recorded NVTX traces.
